title: Blended Cost Methodology v0.9 (Unit Economics Dashboard)
author: Rishi Malhotra
content:
## Purpose
This page sets out how Finance computes **Blended Cost per 1M Output Tokens** (“blended $/1M output tokens”) for Redwood’s internal **Unit Economics Dashboard**. It aims to:
- Give everyone one metric definition that reconciles, within agreed tolerances, to Finance reporting and infrastructure spend inputs.
- Name the source of truth for the GPU cost rate card and describe how it is updated and versioned.
- Fix the allocation rules (including shared overhead and idle capacity) so cross-team analysis rests on the same assumptions.
- List the reconciliation checks and sign-off gates required before numbers go into executive reporting.

This is **v0.9** of the methodology. Changes follow the versioning process below.

## Metric definition (v0.9)
### Primary KPI
**Blended Cost per 1M Output Tokens**

**Formula:**
- **Blended $/1M output tokens** = (Allocated cost in USD / Total output tokens) * 1,000,000

**Unit:** USD per 1,000,000 output tokens.

### What counts as “output tokens”
Included:
- Tokens the model generates and returns to the caller, for both streaming and non-streaming responses.
- Tokens produced for tool/function-call structured outputs when they form part of the model’s generated output.

Excluded:
- Input/prompt tokens.
- Tokens generated internally but never returned because of cancellation, truncation before delivery, or transport errors (unless flagged as delivered; see “Known limitations”).

Token measurement source:
- Platform metering pipeline (token counters emitted by gateway/runtime) aggregated daily.

### Scope of “allocated cost”
Included costs:
- GPU compute cost, applied through the standardized hourly **GPU rate card** (provider/region/capacity type).
- Approved, explicitly listed “serving overhead” adders applied as a percentage of GPU compute (see Overhead policy).

Excluded costs:
- Corporate overhead not attributable to serving (e.g., G&A).
- R&D/training spend.
- One-time incident costs, unless Finance folds them into the rate card for the month/quarter.

## Segmentation and rollups
Drilldowns available in the dashboard:
- **Model** (and version / quantization profile)
- **Region** (normalized canonical region)
- **Customer tier** (self-serve / dedicated / private / enterprise)

Typical Finance rollups:
- Company-wide (all tiers)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
- Region rollup (e.g., NA/EU) for exec narratives

**Important:** The KPI is a blended measure, not a marginal cost. Traffic mix shifts, idle allocation, and rate card changes can move it even when runtime efficiency is unchanged.

## Data sources (sources of truth)
### A) Token denominators
**Source:** Token metering pipeline aggregates (daily)
- Required dimensions: model_id, model_version (or canonical equivalent), region_canonical, customer_tier, streaming_flag, quantization_profile.
- Completeness expectations are tracked by Platform Engineering alongside the aggregation job.

### B) GPU cost inputs
**Source:** Finance GPU cost rate card (versioned)
- Hourly USD rate by:
  - cloud/provider
  - region
  - GPU type (where applicable)
  - capacity type (on-demand vs reserved/committed vs dedicated pool)

**Provenance:** Built from invoices, cloud billing exports, and committed contract schedules.

### C) Capacity accounting / utilization
**Source:** Infra capacity telemetry + scheduler utilization reports
- Used to estimate GPU-hours per segment.
- Utilization drives allocation of shared pools and idle capacity.

### D) Overhead adders
**Source:** Finance-approved overhead policy
- Adders are used only where direct invoiced attribution is unavailable or would be unstable at fine granularity.

## Allocation model
GPU-hours and cost are assigned to segments (model/region/tier) using token-weighted, pool-aware logic.

### 1) Cost pools
Costs are grouped into pools before allocation:
- **Hosted shared pools** (multi-tenant GPU fleets)
- **Dedicated pools** (customer-reserved GPU pools)
- **Private deployments** (customer VPC/on-prem; different cost model)

Each pool has its own allocation rule.

### 2) Allocation basis by pool
#### Hosted shared pools
- Basis: **output tokens by segment** within the pool for the period.
- Segments missing required dimensions (e.g., unknown region) go to “unknown” and are left out of segment drilldowns until fixed. Finance rollups must still include “unknown” so totals are not understated.

#### Dedicated pools
- Basis: **contracted capacity** first, then actual utilization where available.
- Approach:
  - Where dedicated GPU-hours are tracked explicitly: assign them directly to the customer tier/region, then split across models by output token share of that customer’s traffic.
  - Where they are not: allocate on reserved capacity hours from the contract schedule regardless of utilization (see Idle capacity treatment).

#### Private deployments
- Dashboard reporting:
  - Managed private (Redwood bears infra cost): its own pool, allocated like Dedicated.
  - On-prem (customer bears infra cost): **excluded from the GPU cost numerator**; output tokens may appear for product analytics, but Finance KPI reporting excludes these rows so company blended cost is not distorted.

### 3) Idle capacity treatment
Idle capacity is a major driver of blended cost and has to match Finance’s treatment.

Policy:
- **Hosted shared pools:** idle GPU-hours are spread across the pool’s segments in proportion to output tokens (idle cost is blended into unit cost).
- **Dedicated pools:** idle cost stays with the customer’s pool, reflecting the reserved contract. Low traffic means higher unit cost; this is expected.

Rationale:
- Matches Finance’s view of committed capacity: the cost exists whether or not it is used.

### 4) Overhead policy
Overhead is an adder on GPU compute cost per pool:
- Hosted shared pools: +X% (set by Finance each quarter)
- Dedicated pools: +Y% (may differ due to support/ops overhead)
- Private managed: +Z%

The actual percentages live in the rate card version notes rather than on this page.

## Rate card management
### Rate card update cadence
- **Monthly refresh** to stay aligned with invoices and billing.
- **Quarterly lock** for executive KPI decks and board reporting.

### Versioning rules
- Every rate card release carries a version (e.g., 2024Q3, 2024Q4).
- The Unit Economics Dashboard must:
  - Store the rate card version used for each aggregate.
  - Let Finance rerun historical periods with the version that was in effect at the time.

### Effective dates
- Monthly rate updates take effect at the start of the month in UTC unless the release note says otherwise.
- Finance close may use Pacific Time month boundaries; Finance will supply a reporting calendar mapping when needed. Dashboard boundaries stay in UTC.

## Reconciliation methodology
The KPI must be defensible and reconcilable to spend inputs and platform metering.

### Reconciliation checkpoints
1) **Token denominator reconciliation**
   - Compare aggregated output tokens in the unit economics tables with canonical metering totals for the same window.
   - Expected variance: small for stable periods; investigate if > 2%.

2) **Cost numerator reconciliation**
   - Compare allocated GPU cost totals with rate card * GPU-hours pool totals.
   - Expected variance: 0% after deterministic allocation (any gap means missing rows or join/filter bugs).

3) **Spend-to-billing sanity check (monthly)**
   - Compare total allocated compute cost with cloud billing exports/invoices for the month.
   - Tolerance: set by Finance; usually within 3–7% depending on invoice timing, credits, and accruals.

4) **Customer-tier split reasonableness**
   - Check that Hosted/Dedicated/Private pool totals match internal tagging and contract schedules.
   - Spot check a sample of known Dedicated customers each month.

5) **Outlier review**
   - Top-N segments by unit cost and by token volume.
   - Confirm spikes line up with known events (rate changes, utilization drops, region incidents, model rollouts).

### Required artifacts for Finance sign-off
Each monthly/quarterly cycle needs:
- Rate card version and change log
- Reconciliation report (tokens + cost + variances)
- Known data quality incidents for the window, with impact estimates

## Treatment of credits, discounts, and revenue
The metric is **cost-based** and is not netted against:
- customer credits
- pricing discounts
- promotional programs

FP&A may compute contribution margin metrics with revenue separately. Label clearly and do not mix the two in executive narratives.

## Data quality requirements (Finance view)
The KPI is Finance-reportable only when:
- Data for the reporting window has landed on time.
- Dimension completeness meets thresholds (region/model/tier not missing beyond threshold).
- Streaming vs non-streaming token parity checks pass.

If a gate fails, the dashboard either shows a “data confidence” warning and blocks export to the KPI pack, or requires an explicit Finance override with a recorded reason.

## Operational cadence and ownership
- Methodology owner: **FP&A (Rishi Malhotra)**
- Finance sponsor: **CFO (Laura Bennett)**
- Engineering owners:
  - Token metering correctness: **Nadia Rahman / Telemetry & Analytics**
  - Aggregation job + warehouse views: **Logan Wright / Platform Engineering**
  - Dashboard surfaces: **Console & Tooling**

Monthly process:
1) Finance publishes a rate card update (if any)
2) Engineering confirms the new rate card version is ingested
3) Reconciliation report is run and reviewed
4) Finance sign-off is recorded and KPI pack sources are updated

## Known limitations
- Streaming delivery edge cases: when a client disconnects mid-stream, “generated” and “delivered” token counts can diverge depending on the runtime path. We use “delivered” where instrumented and fall back to the runtime counter otherwise. Tracked as an instrumentation gap.
- Private/on-prem cost exclusion: on-prem deployments where the customer pays for infra are excluded from the cost numerator; their tokens may still show for operational visibility.
- Timezone boundary mismatches: the dashboard uses UTC daily rollups; Finance month-close may need different boundaries.

## Change control
Changes to:
- inclusion/exclusion rules
- idle capacity treatment
- overhead adders
- rate card provenance or versioning

are documented as methodology updates and, where material, come with an ADR and a backtest of the impact on prior periods.

## Appendix A: Glossary
- **Output tokens:** tokens returned to the caller as model output.
- **Blended cost:** average cost including idle and shared overhead allocations.
- **Pool:** a group of capacity/cost sharing one allocation rule (hosted shared, dedicated, private).
- **Rate card:** Finance-maintained table mapping capacity inputs to hourly USD cost assumptions.

## Appendix B: Reporting guidance (do’s and don’ts)
Do:
- Label the metric as **blended** and state the time window and rate card version.
- Use drilldowns to find cost drivers (region mix, quant profile changes, caching/batching changes).

Don’t:
- Compare windows without checking for rate card version changes.
- Read a unit cost move as a runtime regression without checking utilization and traffic mix.
